title: Nationwide Flexible Coworking Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT Nationwide Flexible Coworking Services for GSA, PBS. Sources Sought Response Date: October 20th, 2026 4pm CST The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 531120 - Lessors of nonresidential buildings (except miniwarehouses). This Sources Sought Notice is a market research tool being utilized to determine interest and capability of potential sources prior to issuing a formal solicitation, as the solicitation is not available at this time. This IS NOT a Request for Offerors or Proposals. This notice does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for planning purposes only. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are businesses with the requisite capabilities and experience to perform the required work. In addition, this market research is to determine if there are respondents that qualify under one or more socio-economic indicators, including but not limited to, small business, woman-owned business, Women Owned Small business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small business (EDWOSB), Veteran Owned Small business, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small business, SBA Certified Small Disadvantaged business, SBA Certified 8(a) Firm, SBA Certified HUBZone Firm. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) anticipates procuring the services of multiple contractors to perform Flexible Coworking Services, either as shared co-working spaces (Standard coworking spaces where an organization shares the space with other individuals and organizations) or private co-working spaces (Coworking spaces where a certain area (floor, section, private offices with locks) is dedicated to a single organization for federal agencies looking to occupy a coworking space with other federal or private sector employees. It is the intention of GSA to award a multiple contractor, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Description of Services: The firm shall be able to provide flexible coworking space nationwide. The firm shall have an online booking system where Government employees can quickly select a workspace from an online system and/or from a mobile phone application. In addition to having access to both private and shared offices and workstations, Government employees should be able to utilize a meeting room on an hourly or daily basis. The space should be able, if necessary, to be segregated from certain parts of the vendor�s general operations, or at times operate autonomously. The firm shall provide management for each location. Management duties include, but are not limited to providing, uninterrupted internet, office support, oversight for the online booking platform, monthly usage reports to GSA, and billing based on actual usage. Specific management services may vary per location and are subject to localized requirements and offerings. Management does not include IT support for government furnished equipment. Commercial contracting approaches from RFO Part 12 apply to these requirements. If interested in responding to this Sources Sought, please respond by completing and submitting the GSA Flexible Coworking Services Sources Sought Questionnaire no later than 4:00pm Central Standard Time on Tuesday, October 20th, 2026. NO TELEPHONE CALLS WILL BE ACCEPTED. QUESTIONS ARE NOT PERMITTED. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR SOLICITATION.

title: C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control Program (CPCP) Sustaining Engineering and Technical Support Services
description: Request For Information C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control Program (CPCP) Sustaining Engineering and Technical Support Services This Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes pursuant to FAR Part 10. The Government anticipates pursuing a sole-source contract. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation, nor does it represent a commitment or authorization to incur costs on behalf of the United States Government (USG). The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to conduct C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control Program (CPCP). Corrosion prevention and control is defined as the rigorous application of management principles, engineering design and analysis, quality assurance, nondestructive inspection, manufacturing, operations and support technologies, and practices to prevent the initiation of corrosion, avoid functional impairment due to corrosion, and define processes for the tracking and repair of corrosion problems. The Contractor shall provide sustaining engineering and technical support for the C-130 CPCP for the C-130 Hercules Division (AFLCMC/WLN) at Robins Air Force Base (AFB), GA. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support for the strategic planning and oversight of the corrosion program and the ASIP requirements of MIL-STD-1530D. Services include engineering and technical analysis, providing guidance for corrective action, and providing documentation as required for the prevention, control and resolution of corrosion related issues on C-130 aircraft: Developing and providing annual updates to the C-130 Corrosion Prevention and Control (CPC) Plan Conducting annual corrosion assessments of USAF C-130 fleet and operating locations, including evaluation of aircraft, facilities, and maintenance personnel, to include Special Operations Forces (SOF) managed C-130s Performing concept studies and analysis in the identification and definition, preliminary planning, and evaluation of alternative technical approaches for all USAF C-130 aircraft Conducting concept studies and testing for implementation of new coatings, sealants, or other corrosion related products and processes, including test plan development and final report delivery with findings and recommendations to the USAF Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. title: Request for Information/Market Intelligence Notice: Multiple Projects at Vandenberg Space Force Base - Use of Progressive Design Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE: This is a request for information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS CODE: 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 237130 Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD: $45,000,000.00 NOTE: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR based small business regulations, these NAICS codes are provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. PROGRAM/PROJECT OVERVIEW: The 30th Contracting Squadron has multiple infrastructure repair and construction projects planned in Fiscal Year 2027 including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) repair, secure facility renovation, medium-high voltage electrical distribution line repair/replacement, airfield lighting repair, fitness track repair/replacement, and road repair/construction, fire alarm and elevator repair/replacement. The Government is evaluating the feasibility of executing these requirements via Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a in conjunction with the United States Space Force (USSF) Construction Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) at https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/68c3d9f987984f448cd067abaf2950d0/view. Summaries of potential projects being considered for this acquisition strategy are as follows: HVAC Repair: Design and construct the repair and replacement of the HVAC for a multi-tenant office building. Secure Facility Renovation: Design and construction of renovations of a secure facility to meet revised mission requirements Renovation is expected to include wall relocation, electrical, communications, HVAC, and associated finished associated with a facility renovation. Medium-High Voltage Electrical Distribution: Design and construction of the replacement of an aged electrical distribution system ranging from 15kV to 70kV. Airfield Repair: Investigate, design, and construct repairs to various airfield infrastructure to bring it up to current FAA and military airfield code and standards. Outdoor Fitness Track Repair/Replacement: Design and construct repairs to stabilize the soil conditions and repair failing rubberized track surface. Road Repair/Construction: Design and construct road repairs to stabilize subsurface conditions and improve roadways to meet increasing haul capacity and traffic. Fire Suppression and Elevator Repair/Replacement: Design and construct the replacement of a freight elevator for personnel and freight access and the replacement of the existing fire alarm system to include connectivity with the new elevator. INFORMATION REQUESTED: Interested industry partners are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy: Company Profile: Q1. Business Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contract (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. Cage Code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Q10: Which of the seven (7) projects your company may be interested in responding to if the projects are issued as PDB OT Agreements. Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Statutory Compliance: Q11. OTA Experience � Describe your firm�s previous experience, if any, executing projects utilizing OTA. Please select from one of the following: No experience Limited Experience (1 � 5 projects completed) Very Experienced (5+ projects completed) Q12. What project characteristics make PDB OTA particularly advantageous or disadvantageous for these requirements Progressive Design-Build (PDB) / Early Contractor Involvement: Q13. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to submitting a White Paper (Executive Summary, Outline of proposed construction method, estimated schedule, Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price)? Q14. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to a Phase 1 award (Design/Pre-construction) to feel confident in the project's viability? Q15. What collaborative mechanisms (such as joint design charrettes, target-value design workshops, or phased scoping approvals) do you recommend the Government implement in the first 30-90 days to rapidly transition from a "blank page" to a mutually agreed-upon baseline? Q16. Describe your experience executing Progressive Design-Build, Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other highly collaborative delivery methods where designer and builder worked collaboratively with the owner before locking in a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). Q17. Which of the following levels of designs would be the lowest level at which you would feel confident negotiating a GMP? Charrette (basic concept, floor plans, little to no engineering review completed) 35% Design (charrette documentation plus design narrative completed, list of projected codes, UFCs, and disciplines, initial site visit completed by engineering team) 65% Design (35% design documentation plus design analysis including investigation report, explanation of major design decisions, list of specifications, engineering data, environmental surveys) 95% Design (65% design brought to 100% design level except for administrative corrections and engineering stamps) 100% Design (100% complete signed and stamped drawings issued for construction) Feedback on the Acquisition Strategy & Alternatives: Q18. Does the proposed PDB-OTA strategy incentivize your firm to participate? Why or why not? Q19. Are there alternative acquisition strategies, commercial phasing arrangements, or risk-sharing terms that the Government has not considered that would yield a higher quality facility, faster delivery, or lower cost? Bonding Capability: Q20. Specify your maximum bonding (single and aggregate) as a sole prime contractor and/or as a joint venture. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit your responses by 20 October 2026 at 2:00 PM Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) to Jeffrey Grelck at jeffrey.grelck@spaceforce.mil and Alyson Kolding at alyson.kolding@spaceforce.mil The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of these projects under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Upon completion of industry feedback and market intelligence the Government may or may issue a USSF CSO Area of Interest for one, some, all, or none of the projects. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates on thie RFI, however, any subsequent opportunties will be posted separately and not linked to this notice. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

title: Denmark – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Kontrakt om kampagne for en respektfuld politisk debat og forebyggelse af chikane mod politikere
description: Folketinget, KL og Danske Regioner ønsker at udvikle og gennemføre en landsdækkende kampagne, der skal bidrage til en mere respektfuld politisk debat og forebygge chikane mod folkevalgte politikere. Kampagnen skal øge befolkningens forståelse af de demokratiske konsekvenser af chikane mod politikere og samtidig motivere flere borgere til aktivt at reagere, når de møder chikane eller en hadsk tone i den politiske debat. Den valgte leverandør skal udvikle kampagnestrategi, kreativt koncept, budskaber, visuel identitet, medieplan og kampagnematerialer samt stå for produktion, medieindrykning og gennemførelse af kampagnen. Kampagnen skal bygge på eksisterende forskning og målgruppeindsigter og udvikles i tæt samarbejde med Folketinget, KL og Danske Regioner. Opgaven omfatter desuden afprøvning af centrale kampagneelementer, løbende kvalitetssikring og strategiske anbefalinger til, hvordan kampagnen bedst kan skabe effekt og forankres over en flerårig periode. Kampagnen forventes gennemført som en landsdækkende indsats med mulighed for anvendelse på tværs af nationale, regionale og kommunale platforme. Det samlede budget for kampagnen er 2.500.000 DKK ekskl. moms.

description: Nærværende udbudsbekendtgørelse gælder for realisering af den almene boligdel i boligbebyggelsen Agerbæksvej, på adressen Agerbæksvej 13-17A, 8240 Risskov. De kontraktmæssige krav fremgår af fagentreprisekontrakten og vedlagte AB 18 tilføjelser og fravigelser. title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Planung LPh 5-9 Oberflächenabdichtung Deponie Nordost DK I Bereich (Inertfeld), 1. BA
description: Die Entsorgung Dortmund GmbH (EDG) ist u.a. für die Sammlung, Verwertung und Beseitigung der kommunalen und gewerblichen Abfälle verantwortlich. Für die Entsorgung dieser Abfälle wurde die Deponie Dortmund-Nordost 1994 in Betrieb genommen. Die EDG ist beauftragte Dritte des öffentlich-rechtlichen Entsorgungsträgers Stadt Dortmund und gemäß Satzung und Deponiebetriebsvertrag mit der kaufmännischen Sachwaltung des Deponiesondervermögens der Stadt Dortmund sowie der Betriebsführung der Deponie Nordost beauftragt. In dieser Funktion führt die EDG auch die Oberflächenabdichtung der Deponie Nordost durch. Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens sind die Ingenieurleistungen für die Ausführungsplanung, Ausschreibung und Bauüberwachung für den 1. Bauabschnitt des Oberflächenabdichtungssystems im Übergangsbereich von der Bestandsdichtung der Altdeponie Grevel bis auf den Ablagerungsbereich DK I der Deponie Nordost gemäß der 33. Planänderungsgenehmigung vom 30.06.2026 zum Planfeststellungsbeschluss der Deponie Dortmund Nordost vom 09.10.1992. Die EDG sieht vor, die verfüllten Ablagerungsbereiche der Abfälle der Deponieklasse DK I sukzessive endgültig abzudichten.
